description: Nucleoid keeps sign copying live through both zero signs
code:
magnitude = 3
direction = -1
copied = Math.copySign(magnitude, direction)
assert(copied, -3)
magnitude = -7
direction = 1
assert(copied, 7)
magnitude = 0
direction = -0
assert(1 / copied, Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY)
direction = 0
assert(1 / copied, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)
magnitude = 4
copied

description: Nucleoid maintains independent sign copying class rules through deletion and recovery
code:
class Signal(magnitude, direction):
    this.magnitude = magnitude
    this.direction = direction
$Signal.copied = Math.copySign($Signal.magnitude, $Signal.direction)
first = Signal(3, -1)
second = Signal(-7, 1)
assert([first.copied, second.copied], [-3, 7])
first.direction = 1
assert([first.copied, second.copied], [3, 7])
delete first.magnitude
assert(first.copied, undefined)
assert(second.copied, 7)
first.magnitude = -5
assert(first.copied, 5)
[first.copied, second.copied]

description: Nucleoid preserves ignored sign copying argument subscriptions
code:
magnitude = 3
direction = -1
gate = 1
copied = Math.copySign(magnitude, direction, gate)
assert(copied, -3)
delete gate
assert(copied, undefined)
gate = Number.NaN
assert(copied, -3)
direction = 1
assert(copied, 3)
copied

description: Nucleoid intrinsically coerces two sign copying inputs without using extra values numerically
code:
assert(Math.copySign(" -7 ", " -1 "), -7)
assert(Math.copySign(["3"], false), 3)
assert(1 / Math.copySign(null, -0), Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY)
assert(Number.isNaN(Math.copySign()), true)
assert(Number.isNaN(Math.copySign(3)), true)
assert(Number.isNaN(Math.copySign(3, "invalid")), true)
assert(Number.isNaN(Math.copySign(Number.NaN, -1)), true)
assert(Math.copySign(3, -1, Number.NaN, "ignored", {}), -3)
Math.copySign(3, 1)
